Handling requirements for each level are defined in the classification standard, and Strictly Confidential data is restricted to the production environment [2].

rows.note: States all key facts accurately with consistent extra detail.
rows.answer: Yes, we employ the least privilege principle for information system access. Access is role-based, and no one has standing production access; engineers must request just-in-time access via Azure Privileged Identity Management, approved by a second engineer, for up to 4 hours [2]. This practice is consistent with our current Information Security Policy v4.0 [2].

rows.note: Matches key facts; extra policy version detail is fine.
rows.answer: Yes, a process is in place to de-provision access in a timely manner. Access for leavers is revoked within 24 hours of employment termination, and immediately for involuntary terminations, as stated in the current Information Security Policy v4.0 [2]. This aligns with the past 2025 answer, which specified the same timeframe [1].

rows.note: Matches key frequencies; extra details do not contradict.
rows.answer: We complete access reviews quarterly for production and privileged access, and every six months for all other systems, which exceeds the minimum annual requirement [1]. These reviews ensure least privilege and separation of duties are maintained, with just-in-time access enforced for production via Azure PIM and dual approval required for privilege elevation [1]. Access is also revalidated upon significant changes, such as employee termination, with revocation occurring within 24 hours or immediately for involuntary departures [1].

rows.note: States all key facts; extra details do not contradict key.
rows.answer: Yes, we define, implement, and evaluate processes for authenticating access to systems, applications, and data. Multi-factor authentication is mandatory for all workforce accounts using Microsoft Entra ID, with phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2) for privileged accounts [1]. Least privilege is enforced via role-based access control and just-in-time access to production, requiring approval and limited to 4 hours [2]. Customer users can enforce MFA via SSO and WebAuthn [2].

rows.answer: Yes, we define, implement, and evaluate secure credential management processes. Passwords must be at least 14 characters, are checked against breached password lists, and are not subject to periodic forced changes unless compromise is suspected, in alignment with NIST SP 800-63B [1]. Multi-factor authentication is mandatory for all employees and contractors, with phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2) required for privileged accounts [1]. These controls are enforced via Microsoft Entra ID and reviewed as part of our ISO/IEC 27001:2022-certified ISMS [1].

Collection occurs via Microsoft Sentinel, with detection rules enabling continuous monitoring [2].

The plan designates a communications lead for every P1 and P2 incident, mandates notification to affected customers within 24 hours of a confirmed personal data breach via email and phone, and includes updates through our status page [2]. Internal communication occurs via Microsoft Teams, and the plan is reviewed annually, tested through tabletop exercises (most recent March 2026), and updated after significant incidents [5].

The policy also supports reporting for customers subject to DORA by providing necessary incident information [4]. Supply chain breach reporting is not explicitly addressed in the evidence.
